A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with readable and directly matchable methods, equations, experiments, tables and figures. v3 additionally includes Appendices A–C, which are absent from the supplied v2.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark comparisons, architectural ablations, robustness experiments and testing on four real scenes in Section 4.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally reports accuracy by anomaly type and supplementary qualitative results.

M1.justification: The voxel construction, DINOv2 distillation, object extraction, sparse cross-instance attention and training losses remain unchanged. The appendices explain existing procedures without establishing an algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ToysAD-8K, PartsAD-15K and the same four real scenes. The appendix documents existing categories and anomaly families and supplies further examples within that coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Recon-Recog, ImVoxelNet and DETR3D. The appendix's Recons-Recog spelling denotes the existing reconstruction baseline, and Figure A4 illustrates the already discussed ImVoxelNet/DETR3D comparison.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, five-view inputs, model configurations, 50-plus-50 training epochs, object-wise AUC/accuracy and the IoU threshold of 0.5 remain unchanged. Appendix settings provide additional documentation; the anomaly-type breakdown does not establish a revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Figure A3 adds an accuracy breakdown investigating performance across anomaly types, and Figure A4 supplies illustrative baseline failures. The architectural ablations, view-count and object-count analyses, ratio experiment and real-scene testing are retained.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added accuracy chart also presents point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the main robustness results are unchanged; for example, ToysAD-8K-Unseen performance remains 89.15 AUC and 81.57 accuracy. v3 adds dataset histograms, anomaly-type accuracies and qualitative predictions in Figures A1–A6, with some existing examples shown from additional views.

T1.justification: The task assumptions are revised: Section 3 explicitly rejects requiring a normal majority and instead assumes instance-specific anomalous variations alongside highly similar normal instances. Equations (1)–(8) remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v2's abstract defines normal instances as the majority; v3 instead describes inferring a regular reference group and explicitly relaxes the majority requirement. The central contributions remain the same scene-relative task, two benchmarks and cross-instance detection method.

C2.justification: v3 adds specific failure explanations involving low resolution, poor lighting, unresolved occlusion, limited views and transparent objects. Appendix A also discusses collecting real-world training supervision through 2D annotations. Existing synthetic-data, rigidity and camera-pose limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B substantially expand reproducibility information: deformation ranges, mesh normalization, similar-shape retrieval and filtering, camera sampling, rendering assets, category assignments, GPU memory and training times for the model, ablations and baselines. These are newly documented details, not established experimental changes. v3 also removes the abstract's release promise while retaining the same project link.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Looking 3D and distinguishes its supplied 3D reference shape from this work's scene-relative comparison. Three additional references support supplementary discussion and assets. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are reworded, with further edits to related work, dataset descriptions and limitations. An acknowledgment and organized Appendices A–C are added, while the main section sequence and most technical exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table A1 and Figures A1–A6: dataset distributions, accuracy breakdowns, baseline comparison panels and extensive multi-view galleries. This substantially expands the visual presentation. Figures 1–9 retain their content, with accompanying layout and spacing adjustments.

improvement.justification: The new generation parameters and training-cost disclosures improve reproducibility, while Figure A3 adds useful diagnostic evidence to the unchanged principal results. These extend v2's already substantial documentation and experiments. Small new inconsistencies, including Table A1's duplicated category and the Figure A4 discussion's mismatched example count, limit the overall gain.
